title: Polynomial-factor hardness of scheduling unit jobs on prescribed machines
decision_reason: Complete primary formulation, independent July 2026 corroboration, six theorem-scope comparisons, full nearest-statement review, separated A51 self-review and rendering validation passed. No matching unresolved resolution claim located.

problem_fingerprint.input: A finite directed acyclic precedence graph on n jobs and a specified machine M(j) for every job; machine count may vary and empty machines can be removed.
problem_fingerprint.processing: Every job takes exactly one unit of time, without preemption or duplication, on its unique prescribed machine.
problem_fingerprint.feasibility: Nonnegative start times; every precedence edge requires predecessor completion before successor start; jobs on the same machine have disjoint half-open execution intervals.
problem_fingerprint.objective: Minimize makespan, the largest completion time, over feasible schedules.
problem_fingerprint.approximation: An alpha(n)-approximation outputs a feasible schedule of makespan at most alpha(n) times the optimum for every input, in polynomial time in the explicit input size.
problem_fingerprint.target: Prove or disprove existence of an absolute epsilon in (0,1) for which approximation within n^epsilon is NP-hard in the standard polynomial-time reduction sense.
problem_fingerprint.scope: n is the number of jobs, not the number of machines. No fixed machine count, layered-graph promise, communication delays, job release dates or variable processing lengths.
problem_fingerprint.canonical_scope: One power-of-n inapproximability conjecture; constant/polylogarithmic bounds and downstream communication-delay models are not separately counted.

statement_sources.locator: Published §1.1 Conjecture 1.1, §1.3 and §2 Definition 2.1; numbering differs from preprint.
Section 1.1, complete Conjecture 2 and preceding nonpreemptive UMPS model.

independently_authored_corroboration.locator: Section 1, Conjecture 1.1 and Theorems 1.2–1.3; Section 2, Definition 2.1.
independently_authored_corroboration.independence: The three-author July 2026 team is disjoint from the six original authors.
independently_authored_corroboration.scope: Explicitly retains n^epsilon hardness while proving constant-factor NP-hardness and conditional polylogarithmic inapproximability.

second_review.arrangement: Primary-agent research followed by a separated adversarial self-pass; no independent agent or human review.
issues_checked: Published Conjecture 1.1 and preprint Conjecture 2 are the same target; positive exponent is explicit in the independent 2026 restatement.
All processing lengths are one, assignments are prescribed, machine count varies, and n counts jobs. Integer starts suffice by acyclic left-justification.

Constant-factor NP-hardness permits a different fixed reduction for each factor; it does not give a uniform n^epsilon gap. The current polylogarithmic result also uses a quasipolynomial reduction and stronger complexity assumption.
Flexible-assignment delay algorithms and the direction of the UMPS-to-delay reduction do not yield an algorithm for this model.
The complexity conclusion concerns deterministic polynomial-time approximation under P != NP, not an unconditional nonexistence theorem or a claim about randomized algorithms.
second_review.duplicate_check: Nearest full statements 312, 289 and list edge-colouring were compared; unique machine eligibility and a growing approximation gap distinguish this candidate.
second_review.application_check: Fixed-location dependent tasks and worst-case approximation guarantees; no empirical heuristic or efficient-algorithm claim.
second_review.search_limit: Acronym collisions, generic exact scheduling-hardness titles, third-party readers and the original coauthor thesis are discovery only. No new materially matching resolution claim surfaced.

nearest_existing.comparison: Exact complexity for three interchangeable processors. UMPS fixes a unique eligible machine per job, lets the machine count vary, and asks for n^epsilon approximation hardness.
Beat factor two for variable assignment-dependent processing times without precedence. UMPS has fixed assignments, unit lengths and an arbitrary precedence DAG.
Two simultaneous resources per job and availability lists; an exact existence guarantee. UMPS uses one prescribed resource with precedence and a complexity-theoretic gap.

source_records.title: Scheduling Under Non-Uniform Job and Machine Delays
source_records.version: Published proceedings PDF; extended arXiv source not independently compared.
source_records.locator: Title and metadata; §1.1 Definition 1, full Theorems 1–4 and accompanying model discussion, pp.98:3–98:6.
source_records.read: Additive endpoint-delay algorithms versus arbitrary job-machine delay hardness reduction. The guarantees retain their duplication and additive-delay qualifications. Theorem 4 is a reduction from UMPS, not an algorithm for it.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: For each fixed gamma>1, gamma approximation is NP-hard.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: A separate fixed-parameter reduction for each constant is not a uniform power-of-job-count gap.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: A (log N)^gamma gap for some gamma>0, with a quasipolynomial-time reduction and NP-not-in-deterministic-quasipolynomial-time assumption.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Both gap growth and reduction time differ from the proposed n^epsilon NP-hardness under polynomial reductions.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Logarithmic UMPS hardness inherited from job shop with variable processing lengths.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Does not establish the unit-length power-of-n target.

resolution_comparisons.locator: Conjecture 1.2 and Theorem 1.2; preprint Conjecture 3 and Theorem 4
resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Conditional related-machine scheduling hardness from a companion UMPS conjecture restricting machine count.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: A conditional implication is not an unconditional proof of the candidate; no second entry is counted for the companion.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Algorithms with flexible job assignment for delays decomposing into endpoint contributions; some permit duplication/additive rho_max.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Arbitrary prescribed machine assignments are not part of their input model. Setting delays to zero removes delay restrictions, not the UMPS eligibility constraints.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Polynomial-time approximation-preserving reduction from UMPS to arbitrary job-machine delay scheduling.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Transfers hardness to a different model; does not prove the conjectured hardness of the source problem or provide an algorithm for it.
